title: Microsoft Teams: report a message or an external user for a security concern in US Government clouds
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, reporting controls and qualified licensing statements are supported. Minor corrections should carry through a reporting-dialog qualification and acknowledge that the Teams reporting reference also excludes Government clouds.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes Teams users reporting suspicious messages.
claims.quote: Users in Gov clouds can now report suspicious messages and external users within Teams.

claims.where: summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap describes Teams users reporting suspicious external users.
claims.quote: Users in Gov clouds can now report suspicious messages and external users within Teams.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap says reports surface in the Teams admin center for administrators to investigate and act.
claims.quote: Reports are surfaced in the Teams admin center, giving admins greater visibility into potentially malicious activity and enabling them to investigate and take appropriate action.

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Android, Desktop, iOS, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.where: title; front matter: clouds; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists GCC, GCC High and DoD for this Government-cloud rollout.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.where: front matter: previewDate
claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn documents reporting a chat or channel message through More options > Report this message > Security concern.
claims.quote: Go to chat or channel message and select … > Report this message. ... Select Security concern.

claims.where: What's changing: Defender reporting label
claims.claim: The Defender instructions label the reporting selection Security risk - Spam, phishing, malicious content.
claims.quote: If reporting for Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance is turned off, users might not have the dropdown list to select Security risk - Spam, phishing, malicious content. Instead, they're shown a confirmation pop-up.
claims.fix: After the sentence giving the Defender label, add: 'Those instructions also say that if reporting for Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance is turned off, users might see a confirmation pop-up instead of the selection.' Keep the existing submissions-teams citation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can report an external user from an external chat request by selecting Report this person while blocking them.
claims.quote: Open the external chat request. ... follow the prompt to block the user. ... Click Report this person checkbox and confirm.

claims.where: What's changing: external user profile card
claims.claim: Users can report an external user from the user's profile card while blocking the contact.
claims.quote: Open the user's profile card. ... Open the menu option and select Block contact ... Click Report this person checkbox and confirm.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1]; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can review reported chat and channel messages and external users in User reported security submissions.
claims.quote: The User reported security submissions report in the Microsoft Teams admin center helps you review security-related reports submitted by users in your organization.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The report has Calling, Chats and channels, and User categories.
claims.quote: Under Report category, choose one of the following categories: Calling; Chats and channels; User

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The admin center report supports CSV export.
claims.quote: You can export these reports to a CSV file for further analysis.

claims.where: What's changing: cloud disagreement
claims.claim: The two cited Teams reporting pages do not name a cloud.
claims.quote: Searched: cloud, GCC, Government and DoD in the complete End user reporting for Security and User reported security submissions report pages; neither page names a cloud.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The Defender reporting page says user reporting of calls, meetings and messages is unsupported in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: User reporting of calls, meetings, and messages in Teams is not supported in U.S. Government organizations (Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High, and DoD).

claims.where: What's changing: cloud note and external users
claims.claim: The Government exclusion note on the Defender reporting page does not mention external users.
claims.quote: Searched: external users in the Government exclusion note on submissions-teams; its listed items are calls, meetings and messages, not external users.

claims.where: What's changing: roadmap is the later statement
claims.claim: The roadmap record is later than the cited Defender page's cloud exclusion.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default specifically for this Government-cloud rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Report a security concern' GCC default; 569609 default. Read roadmap, end-user-reporting-security and submissions-teams. General Learn says on by default, but the Government exclusion leaves its applicability to this rollout unresolved.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The cited Teams page gives Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Report a security concern.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Messaging policies. ... Select a policy. ... Turn on the setting: Report a security concern.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting $true enables the security-reporting policy setting.
claims.quote: -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting: This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Roles
claims.claim: Learn requires Global Administrator or Teams Administrator to view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the Global Administrator or Teams Administrator roles.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: newer route
claims.claim: Learn identifies Settings & policies as the entry to the policy in the new experience.
claims.quote: To access this policy in the new experience, go to Settings & policies.

claims.where: controls[0].note: cloud availability
claims.claim: The cited setting documentation does not specify the cloud availability of this policy setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Report a security concern' GCC default and 'AllowSecurityEndUserReporting' external. Read end-user-reporting-security, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy and submissions-teams; no setting-specific Government availability is given.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; What's changing: report availability
claims.claim: The report is reached through Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. ... On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.
claims.fix: In the cloud-disagreement paragraph add: 'The Teams reporting reference also lists User reported security submissions as unavailable in GCC, GCC High and DoD, in contrast to the roadmap.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-analytics-and-reports/teams-reporting-reference#teams-reporting-reference, whose report row reads Public Yes, GCC No, GCCH No, DoD No, and add that URL to sources.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls; Open questions: API or export feed
claims.claim: No API or automated export feed for this report was found; its page documents the admin view and CSV export.
claims.quote: Searched: 'User reported security submissions' API; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph 'security submissions' Teams; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell 'user reported security' Teams. Read report page and Graph threatSubmission beta; no API for this report found.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The user's messaging policy must enable Report a security concern for chat, channel and external-user reporting.
claims.quote: For chat and channel messages and external users, the Report a security concern setting must be turned on in the user's messaging policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The chat and channel report CSV includes a sender-domain field.
claims.quote: Sender domain name: Domain of the sender. This field might be blank if the sender uses a consumer account, depending on their privacy setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The exported chat and channel participant list has a maximum of 20 entries.
claims.quote: Maximum 20 entries: up to 10 entries from the reporter's tenant and up to 10 entries from non-reporter tenants.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The chat and channel CSV includes reporter comments when supplied.
claims.quote: Reporter comments: Optional comments that the reporter user sent along with the report, if any. ... Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External-user reports contain the reported user's display name and email address if available.
claims.quote: Reported user name: Reported user's display name and email address, if available. If the reported user uses a consumer account, their email address might not be available depending on their privacy setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure: submission to Microsoft
claims.claim: The Defender page says message content is copied when an applicable Teams item is reported to Microsoft.
claims.quote: When a user reports a Teams item to Microsoft, the following data associated with the item is copied and included in ongoing algorithm reviews, as applicable: Message content.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure: contextual messages
claims.claim: Up to fifteen messages before and after the reported message might be shared for analysis.
claims.quote: Specifically, up to fifteen messages before and after the reported message might also be shared for analysis.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: Government submissions
claims.claim: The sources do not establish whether the Microsoft-analysis sharing behaviour applies to reports from this Government rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams security concern government reporting Microsoft analysis data GCC. Read submissions-teams, submissions-admin and mdo-gov; Teams Government reporting is excluded on the Defender page, and the admin-submission Government analysis rule concerns email.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The reported-user identifier can be used by administrators to block that user on the Teams admin center External Access page.
claims.quote: Reported user ID: Microsoft Resource Identifier (MRI) of the reported user. Admins can use this identifier when blocking the user on the External Access page of the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Message senders are not notified that their messages were reported.
claims.quote: Message senders aren't notified their messages were reported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users initiate reports and administrators review and export the submitted reports.
claims.quote: The User reported security submissions report in the Microsoft Teams admin center helps you review security-related reports submitted by users in your organization. You can export these reports to a CSV file for further analysis.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Administrator blocking of the reported user is a separate action from reviewing the report.
claims.quote: Admins can use this identifier when blocking the user on the External Access page of the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can report the same item more than once.
claims.quote: Users can report the same items multiple times.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn says Defender supports message reporting but not external-user reporting, which is reviewed in the Teams report instead.
claims.quote: Only user reporting of messages is supported in Microsoft Defender as of now. User reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Teams reporting page describes the capability for organizations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The Defender reporting page additionally lists Defender for Office 365 Plan 1.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: report prerequisites
claims.claim: The report page's prerequisites name reporting settings and submitted reports, not a licence requirement.
claims.quote: Reported interactions appear ... only after users submit reports. ... Users can submit reports only when the required reporting settings are enabled in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Defender plans available as add-ons or within subscriptions such as Microsoft 365 E5.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2 (add-on licenses or included in subscriptions like Microsoft 365 E5), admins can also see user reported messages in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A licence entitlement specifically covering this Government reporting rollout is not yet established in the documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams user reported Government licensing; Defender Office 365 service description Teams user reporting government licensing. Read reporting pages, mdo-gov and Defender service description; general Government licences are published, but not entitlement to this excluded reporting case.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No price or meter specific to this Government reporting feature is published in the sources found.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reporting GCC price; Teams report Gov licensing. Read submissions-teams, submissions-admin, mdo-gov and Defender for Office 365 service description; no feature-specific Government reporting price or meter found.

claims.where: Governance controls: two settings
claims.claim: For messages, the Teams reporting toggle and the Defender reporting setting must both be enabled for reports to appear on Submissions > User reported.
claims.quote: If "Report a security concern" is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported messages to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Not a security concern lets users report messages incorrectly flagged as malicious.
claims.quote: Users can report messages in Teams chats or channels that are incorrectly flagged by Link Protection as containing malicious URLs. ... In the report dialog that opens, select Not a security concern.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: No Message Center post was supplied for this item.
claims.quote: Searched: the supplied pre-check, roadmap record and writer output for a Message Center post or message_center_post evidence block; none was supplied.
